title: Roadmap lattice sync notes (prep + follow-ups)
content:
Goal: get product + eng + applied ML on the same page about Q2 waveform: tradeoffs between latency SLO tightening, quantization rollout, and model flavor parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Meeting objectives (30–40m):
- Quick status (3m each): Product, Eng infra, Applied ML
- Resolve gating decisions for the streaming latency initiative (10m) — which routes get low-latency priority vs. batching-first?
- Align on quantization rollout plan & fallback variants (10m) — prod readiness checklist, safety net.
- Clear action items and owners (5–10m).

Prep notes / context (do not read verbatim):
- Product (Priya): customers asking for 50–100ms tail improvements on short-chat flows; adoption sensitive to 1) predictable latency and 2) deterministic fallbacks. We should aim to reduce 95p by 20% for short-seq routes.
- Eng infra (Ravi): infra can reserve burst lanes on Dedicated (configurable) and expose route-level policies, but needs explicit route tagging + quotas. Risk: increasing reserved lanes reduces overall throughput/cost efficiency.
- Applied ML (Miguel): quantized 4-bit variant (q4f) shows ~1.6x throughput but subtle hallucination deltas on our eval set; we need a canary that runs quality checks with existing prompts. Also investigating finer KV cache strategies for chat to avoid re-computation on short-turn dialogs.

Open questions I want us to answer in the sync:
- Which routes (by product name + api route) are candidates for low-latency lanes? (target: <6 routes to start)
- Do we require automatic fallback to float16 when regression detected, or manual rollback?
- What acceptance thresholds for qa/regression on canary (pass/fail metrics + sample prompts)?
- Timeline: soft rollout window (2 weeks) vs. hard SLA (1 month)

Proposed concrete decisions (to bring to meeting):
1) Pick 4 priority routes: chat.short, chat.streaming, embedding.fast, rerank.preview. (if everyone agrees)
2) Enable reserved low-latency lane on Dedicated for those routes with 10% capacity; monitor cost delta weekly; auto-scale up to 25% if 95p latency > target.
3) Canary quantized model policy: deploy q4f alongside fp16 for 48h, run automated eval harness (see linked CI) every 6h, block promotion if quality delta > 1.5% on intent+factuality suite.

Notes-to-self / friction points to surface:
- Priya will likely push for faster rollout; emphasize need for concrete rollback criteria.
- Ravi will push back on reserved capacity %; prepare a cost sensitivity table (baseline vs +10% reserved vs +25%). TODO: sketch numbers before meeting.
- Miguel needs a small labeled prompt set (~200 prompts) to run the canary; volunteer to assemble 80% from existing eval repo and 20% new customer examples.

Action items (post-meeting template — fill during sync):
- [Owner] Task — [Due] — [Notes/acceptance]
- Siena: compile cost sensitivity quick table for reserved lanes — 2026-04-02 — include 95p delta and monthly $ delta
- Ravi: prepare minimal config spec for route tagging + autoscale policy — 2026-04-01 — include API shape and example CLI
- Miguel: generate canary prompt set and add to CI harness (automated checks) — 2026-04-03 — list of 200 prompts in repo and pass criteria
- Priya: confirm product route priorities and customer contact list for beta — 2026-04-01 — will confirm which customers to invite
- Avery: add metric dashboards (95/99 latency, cost per token, quality regression) to Redwood Console mock dashboard — 2026-04-04

Meeting facilitation checklist (Siena):
- Start on time; 30–40m; keep each status update to 3m; use timer.
- Collect decisions in Google Doc (this file) and paste final action items to Jira epic and Confluence page.
- If we hit a hard blocker (e.g., can't agree on rollback), surface to exec prompt ops for decision within 48h.

Draft email to attendees (copy into calendar):
- Subject: Quick sync: roadmap lattice — latency lanes, quantization canary (30m)
- Agenda: status (3m each), decisions on routes/reserved lanes, canary gating, action items
- Deliverable: owner-assigned action items + timeline

Stuff to link in meeting:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ROADMAP-2026 (overview)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-1427 (latency-lanes epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981 (route-tagging prototype)

After-sync follow-ups (how I want to run it):
- Within 24h: paste notes + decisions to Confluence, create Jira subtasks for each action item, ping owners.
- 2 weeks: sanity check demo from eng + canary quality report from Miguel.
- 4 weeks: roll vs rollback decision point; if quality stable and latency improved, promote to wider rollout.

Quick local checklist (things I need to prepare before meeting):
- cost sensitivity table (stub) — DONE? in progress
- draft email and calendar invite — DONE
- assemble existing eval prompt subset — TODO (Miguel will help)
- example reserved-lane YAML + CLI snippet — TODO (ask Ravi for example)

Random scratch / friction ideas (brain dump):
- Could we expose a "latency-priority" tag on routes that is policy-only (no committed capacity) for Hosted API customers to opt into? Might be a premium feature.
- Consider a lightweight regression harness that runs on top of streaming responses (token-level ROUGE + hallucination heuristics) to detect quality drift fast.

Unresolved / parking lot:
- Pricing model for reserved lanes for small-mid customers.
- Legal implications of routing customer data across Dedicated vs Hosted for burst fallback.

End notes: keep this very pragmatic; goal is to get a minimal safe rollout that proves latency gains without costing us quality. Read the PR and Jira before the sync.
